fix(Grace Notes): Fix grace note fingering positioning for multiple grace notes with fingering (PR #1642)

code by @isc / Claude, thanks!

* fix: calculate fingering collision offsets per voice entry for grace notes

Grace notes are rendered at different horizontal positions, so their
fingering collision offsets should be calculated separately for each
voice entry (chord), not across all notes in the staff entry.

Before this fix, sequential grace notes or grace note chords would have
incorrect fingering positions because the collision detection included
notes from other voice entries at different X positions.

fix(Octave Bracket): Fix octave shift not applied to grace notes before stop direction (PR #1649)

* fix: octave shift not applied to grace notes before stop direction

When an octave-shift stop is placed after grace notes in MusicXML,
the grace notes were not receiving the octave shift. This happened
because addOctaveShift used previousFraction as end timestamp, but
previousFraction is only updated for real notes, not grace notes.

The fix uses currentFraction instead (like addPedalMarking already
does) and introduces endVoiceEntryIndex on OctaveShift to distinguish
grace notes before vs after the stop when they share the same
timestamp. The visual bracket (dashed line) now also extends to the
last covered grace note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix octave shift bracket not ending correctly on multi-system shifts

When an octave shift spans multiple staff lines and the stop falls
between grace notes, the visual bracket (TextBracket) on the ending
system was not receiving the endVoiceEntryIndex. This caused the
dashed line to extend past the intended stop point to the last
voice entry at that timestamp.

Pass endVoiceEntryIndex to setEndNote in the multi-system loop,
matching the existing behavior for single-system shifts.

fix(Tuplet): Align cross-staff tuplet notes with simultaneous notes in other voices (PR #1676)

* fix(Tuplet): Fix cross-staff tuplet notes horizontally misaligned with simultaneous notes in other voices

When a tuplet voice is split across staves (e.g. a left-hand triplet whose
top note is notated on the upper staff), the staff missing a tuplet member
fills that slot with a ghost note. VexFlowConverter.GhostNotes() decomposed the
gap with durations(frac, false), i.e. a greedy decomposition into standard
note-value rests. A tuplet member such as a triplet eighth (1/12 of a whole
note) is not a dyadic fraction and cannot be represented exactly that way, so
the decomposition overshoots (1/12 -> 1/16 + 1/64 + 1/128 = 11/128). The
voice's accumulated ticks then drift and every following note is pushed out of
vertical alignment with simultaneous notes in other voices.

This is the cross-staff/ghost-note counterpart of the StaveNote tuplet tick
fix (PR #1631): for a non-dyadic gap, emit a single ghost note whose ticks
match the gap exactly (frac * VF.RESOLUTION, kept as an exact rational),
instead of the overshooting dyadic rest decomposition. The dyadic path is
unchanged.

Adds a cross-staff triplet sample and unit tests asserting the ghost filler
length and beat-2 cross-voice tick alignment.

fix(Notes): Don't stagger/x-shift a unison between two voices in a three-voice stave (PR #1677)

* fix(Notes): Don't stagger a unison between two voices in a three-voice stave

In a three-voice stave, ModifierContext.formatNotes shifts the middle voice
right whenever it "intersects" the upper or lower voice. That generic rule also
fired when the intersection was a unison (the middle voice on the same staff
line as another voice), pushing two identical pitches apart even though they
should share one horizontal position (overlapping noteheads). The two-voice
path already handles unisons this way (it doesn't stagger same-shape unisons);
this brings the three-voice path in line.

Only suppress the shift for a *mergeable* unison - same staff line, single
noteheads, matching notehead shape (not one half/whole and the other not) and
matching dot count - mirroring the two-voice stagger conditions. Genuine
collisions (e.g. a second) are still staggered.

Adds a three-voice sample (unison on beat 1, second-interval collision on
beat 2) and unit tests asserting the unison overlaps while the second still
staggers.

* fix(Notes): Prioritise a three-voice unison over a nearby bass voice

The first version only suppressed the middle-voice stagger when the very
intersection that triggered it was a unison. But the middle voice can be a
unison with the upper voice while also sitting close to the lower voice (e.g. a

* feat(Notes): Add EngravingRules.StaggerDottedUnisons to merge dot-differing unisons

A unison between two voices on the same staff line is meant to share one
horizontal position (overlapping noteheads), and mergeableUnison() already does
this for notes of the same shape. It made one exception: if the two notes differ
in dot count it kept them staggered, even though their noteheads have the same

differ only in dot count overlaps like any other unison; the notehead-shape guard
(half/whole vs not) and StaggerSameWholeNotes are unchanged.

fix(Performance): Round staffline/system distances to half pixels for consistent staff line anti-aliasing (#1681, #937)

The pixel-based skyline calculation produced values quantized to pixels, so the
skyline-derived staffline and system distances always landed on half-pixel positions,
giving the (1px) staff lines one of two consistent anti-aliasing phases (a crisp
single pixel row, or two half-covered rows). The geometric calculation's exact values
propagated arbitrary fractional positions, making the staff line weight vary visibly
from system to system (and from the previous releases' renderings).

Rounding the two skyline-derived distances (between stafflines and between systems)
to half pixels restores the previous behavior. No change for pixel-based skyline
values, which are already half-pixel-quantized.

Note this restores the previous *phase set*: which of the two phases a system gets can
still differ from previous renderings where the (exact) skyline extremes differ from
the pixel-quantized ones by more than a quarter pixel.

feat(Performance): Snap stafflines to crisp pixel positions: new EngravingRule SnapStafflinesToCrispPixels, default true (#1681, #937)

The 1px staff lines render as a crisp single pixel row when their centers lie at
half-pixel positions, and as two half-covered (gray-ish) rows when they lie exactly
between pixel rows. Staffline and system y positions are derived from skyline values,
so previous releases produced a per-system mix of both phases that changed whenever
the layout shifted sub-pixel; with the geometric skyline calculation's exact values,
even arbitrary in-between phases. This showed up as seemingly bolder or lighter
staff lines per system, e.g. as confusing diffs in visual regression tests.

With SnapStafflinesToCrispPixels (default true), staffline distances within a system
are rounded to whole pixels, and each system's y position is snapped (by at most half
a pixel) so that all staff lines render crisply - consistent for every system, every
release, and both skyline calculation methods. The page-level shift of all systems by
the first system's BorderTop in MusicSheetCalculator is rounded accordingly, since it
would otherwise undo the snap. Exact at zoom 1 (and integer multiples), within a page.

When disabled, the previous behavior remains, with the skyline-derived distances
rounded to the half-pixel granularity that the pixel-based skyline calculation
produced naturally (so the line weight at least stays in the two known phases).

refactor(Performance): No static state in GeometricSkyBottomLineContext: caches owned by EngravingRules (#1681, #937)

The text measurement canvases, character ink extents and flattened glyph outline
caches were static, i.e. shared between all OSMD instances on a page. They are pure

independent (e.g. if such values ever become configurable per instance), and so

contexts (tools, tests) get their own private cache instance. The constants became
private readonly fields and the pure isTransparent() helper a module function,
leaving the class without any statics; the GeometricSkyBottomLineContext class is now
the first declaration in the file, with the helper class and interfaces at the bottom.

fix(AutoResize): Don't re-render the first loaded sheet a second time (#1684, #1683, #1681 follow-up)

The resize handler fired its callbacks once when attached (via immediate timers),

was a no-op anyway) - so only fire them in that case (RenderCount > 0).

feat(Slur): Render cross-staff slurs, e.g. left hand to right hand (#1006)

Cross-staff slurs - a slur starting on a note in one staff and ending on a
note in another staff of the same instrument (e.g. bass clef to treble clef
for piano) - were not rendered at all. Two separate problems were fixed:

1. Parsing (SlurReader): MusicXML writes the end note's staff before the
   start note's staff (separated by a <backup>), so the slur's "stop" was
   read before its "start". SlurReader only handled start-before-stop and
   silently dropped the slur. It now links the slur to its notes regardless
   of the order in which the two ends are read.

2. Curve calculation (GraphicalSlur): the slur spans two stafflines stacked
   vertically, so its curve cannot be computed by the usual single-staffline
   code (which also runs before the final vertical staff positions are known).
   New GraphicalSlur.calculateCurveCrossStaff() computes the curve at draw
   time - when both stafflines have their final positions - as a bezier that
   bows out from the line between the two notes. The slur is attached to the
   start note's staffline and kept out of the per-staff open/close machinery
   so it does not spawn phantom continuation slurs on following stafflines.

test(SkyBottomLine): Fix CI/Linux test failure: Stabilize the geometric/raster parity test under a first-render scrollbar (#1681, #937)

The geometric-vs-raster skyline comparison renders each method once on the same container and
requires their staffline widths (i.e. skyline array lengths) to match. OSMD derives the page width
from the container's offsetWidth at render time. The first render of a tall sheet runs before a
vertical scrollbar exists, so it sees the full container width; that render makes the content exceed
the viewport height, the browser adds a vertical scrollbar, and the container's content width shrinks
by the scrollbar width (~12px with classic scrollbars). The second render reads the smaller width, so
the page width - and thus every system width and every skyline array length - differs between the two
renders.

On Linux/Firefox this shifted the page width by 1.2 units (133.8 -> 132.6), so the two captures
disagreed on staffline 0's length (352 vs 349; all systems drift, staffline 0 just asserts first).
Browsers with overlay scrollbars that reserve no width (e.g. Firefox on Windows) didn't show it. It is
a DOM container-size feedback, not covered by the per-render VexFlow state resets.

Reserve the vertical scrollbar up front (documentElement.style.overflowY = "scroll") so the container
width - and thus the page width - is the settled width from the very first render, holding the layout
fixed across the two captures so they differ only in the skyline method under test.

Verified on Firefox 151/Linux: without the reserve it fails 352 vs 349, with it the test passes.

feat(rendering): add incremental "system by system" rendering (renderNext API, #1604, #1554)

Render large scores progressively instead of blocking on one full render(), for
faster first paint. The sheet is laid out as a growing prefix and only the
newly-stable systems are drawn into a single shared backend, appended below what
is already on screen. Works for the endless vertical-scroll page format and for
RenderSingleHorizontalStaffline (one staffline growing to the right).

Public API (OpenSheetMusicDisplay):
- renderNext(options?: { measures?: number, systems?: number }): IRenderNextResult
  -- render and append the next batch. By default it advances ~8 visual measures (a
  multi-rest counts as one); pass `systems` to advance by whole music systems (lines)
  instead, ending each batch exactly on a system boundary (#1604). `systems` is
  vertical only -- a single horizontal staffline is one system, so it ignores
  `systems` and uses `measures`. The first call auto-starts a fresh session (clears,
  lays out from measure 0); later calls append. Returns progress { done,
  renderedMeasures, totalMeasures, lastRenderedMeasure, nextUnrenderedMeasure } where
  the measure handles are the GraphicalMeasure[] across all staves at that position.
- renderRemaining() -- finish synchronously (e.g. before PDF/image export).
- resetIncrementalRendering() -- abandon a session; auto-called by render()/reset().
- IncrementalRenderingActive / IncrementalRenderingComplete / IncrementalRenderProgress.
- enableIncrementalRenderingOnScroll(options? & { scrollElement? }) /
  disableIncrementalRenderingOnScroll() -- passive scroll-to-load near the edge
  (page bottom for vertical, right edge for single-horizontal), rAF fill, and
  auto-detach on completion.

How it works:
- Vertical (renderAppendGrowing): re-lays the whole prefix each batch (the greedy
  builder is forward-stable), draws only the new systems, defers the prefix's last
  (unstretched) system, and reconciles if a growing layout moves an earlier system.
- Horizontal (renderAppendGrowingHorizontal): single growing system at
  SheetMaximumWidth; single-staff grows the laid-out prefix, multi-staff lays the
  whole score out once and reuses it (only the drawn x-window grows) so lower
  stafflines never drift.
- Skyline reuse cache (gated by EngravingRules.LazyConsistentGraphic) reuses stable
  interior systems' sky/bottom lines across batches, turning the per-batch
  O(prefix) skyline pass into O(new systems). Off for a normal render().
- Drawer x-window / system-index gates draw each element exactly once; inert at
  their +/-Infinity / -1 defaults, so a normal render() is unaffected.
- Canvas backend snapshots and redraws its bitmap on resize (a canvas resize clears
  it); the SVG backend grows in place.

All gates and caches are gated behind LazyConsistentGraphic (forced false by
render()) or are no-ops at their defaults, so normal rendering is unchanged. Demo:
an "Incremental rendering (load on scroll)" toggle plus a renderRemaining() guard
before PDF export.

Verified renderNext() output multiset-identical to a normal render() on
Bach / Gounod / Actor, both vertical and single-horizontal.

fix(IncrementalRendering): Don't jump to top on mobile when scroll-loading more (#1690, #1554)

When lazy/incremental rendering (renderNext / enableIncrementalRenderingOnScroll)
loaded the next batch as the user scrolled, the page jumped back to the top on
mobile/touch devices, while staying put on desktop with mouse-wheel scrolling.

Root cause: the scroll handler appended each batch via renderNext() without
preserving the scroll offset. Within a batch, when an already-drawn system shifts
slightly as the prefix grows (someDrawnSystemMoved), renderAppendGrowing takes the
reconciliation path and calls createOrRefreshRenderBackend(), which removes the
rendered SVG/Canvas from the container (removeAllChildrenFromContainer) before the
new, taller backend is sized in. While the page height is momentarily collapsed,
mobile/touch browsers clamp the scroll offset to the top, whereas desktop browsers
restore it -- hence the platform-specific symptom.

Fix: in enableIncrementalRenderingOnScroll's onScroll handler, capture the scroll
target's offset before renderNext() and restore it afterwards, once the page is at
its new (taller) height. Unlike renderAndScrollBack(), which restores by percent
(suited to a same-height re-render), this restores the ABSOLUTE offset: the appended
systems are below the viewport and must not shift it. Both axes are restored, so the
RenderSingleHorizontalStaffline (horizontal scroll) mode is covered too. The !==
guards make it a no-op when the browser did not move the offset, so desktop behavior
is unchanged.

Long, steep slurs (e.g. in Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata at certain canvas widths) arced far higher
than the notes/objects they span: the cubic bezier's apex grows with the slur width and overshoots

flattened into near-straight lines.

- SlurFlattenToObstacleMargin (default 3)

* fix(Ties): match tied notes by sounding pitch instead of letter name

Enharmonic ties (e.g. F# tied to Gb, as MuseScore 4 exports) were
dropped or mis-bound because tie matching compared FundamentalNote
(letter name) rather than sounding pitch. Add a half-tone fallback in
findCurrentNoteInTieDict(): the exact FundamentalNote+Octave match runs

* fix(Ties): keep the accidental on the continued note of an enharmonic tie

An enharmonic tie (e.g. F#–Gb, #1694) connects two different spellings of one
sounding pitch, so unlike a same-spelling tie the continued note carries its
own accidental. AccidentalCalculator suppressed the accidental on every
continued tie note, which dropped the second note's accidental for enharmonic
ties — F#–Gb rendered as F#–G. Suppress only when the tied notes share
fundamental note and accidental; otherwise let the continued note draw its own.

Extends the #1694 render test to assert the tied end note keeps its flat.

* fix(Ties): distinguish enharmonic tie respellings by letter name only

Addresses the #1695 review regression. The first fix compared both letter and
accidental, so a same-letter tie whose accidental enum differed — e.g. an
explicit B natural tied to an implied B under a Bb key signature (Telemann
m.9–10) — fell through and drew an unnecessary natural on the continued note.

A tie always joins one sounding pitch, so the only thing that varies is the
spelling: same letter name (FundamentalNote) means the same written note held
on (keep the accidental suppressed, as before); a different letter name is a
genuine enharmonic respelling (F#–Gb) whose continued note must draw its own
accidental. Compare by FundamentalNote only.

Adds a Telemann-based regression test asserting no continued tie note redraws a
natural, alongside the F#–Gb enharmonic test.

fix(Layout): Fix misaligned voices with dotted durations. Align voices when a note's type and dots disagree with its duration (PR #1697)

* fix(VexFlowMeasure): align voices when type+dots disagree with duration

VexFlow derives a note's ticks from its displayed type and dots. When a
MusicXML note or rest has a <type> (+<dot>s) that does not match its
actual <duration> (e.g. an invisible rest written as a dotted half that
only lasts 2.5 quarters), the tick counting of the vexflow voice drifts
and every following note in that voice is drawn horizontally misaligned
against simultaneous notes of the other voices, looking like a separate
rhythmic event instead of part of the same beat.

Generalize the existing tuplet tick correction to any such mismatch by
overwriting the vexflow ticks with the actual model duration
(graphicalNoteLength). Whole measure rests and grace notes keep their
original ticks to avoid unnecessary spacing changes.

* fix(layout): align voices when a note's type and dots disagree with its duration

When a note or rest is encoded with a <type> (plus <dot>s) that does not
match its actual <duration> — a common pattern for invisible rests filling
irregular gaps, e.g. type=half with a dot but a duration of only 2.5
quarters — the VexFlow StaveNote is built from the type and dots, so the
tick counting of that voice drifts. Every subsequent note of the voice is
then drawn misaligned against the other voices: two simultaneous notes end
up in separate columns, looking like sequential notes.

Generalize the tick correction that was already applied to tuplets:
whenever the VexFlow ticks disagree with the note's graphicalNoteLength,
rewrite them exactly via VF.Fraction. Whole-measure rests keep their
vexflow whole-rest ticks (nothing follows them in the voice) and grace
notes are excluded; the tuplet branch behaves as before.

Adds a minimal test sample with a bug measure and a control measure that
must render identically.

fix(RepetitionInstructionReader): Don't misread texts mentioning D.S. etc. as repetition instructions, e.g. "voice tacet on D.S." (#1687). Only detect an instruction if the whole text is the instruction

Previously, a <words> text that merely contained an instruction keyword
(d.s., d.c., dal segno, da capo, to coda, fine, coda, segno) as a
separate word anywhere was consumed as a repetition instruction:
the text was not rendered at all, and an incorrect repetition (jump)
was created. Now words are only detected as an instruction if the
entire text is the instruction (trailing periods/spaces allowed),
analogous to MuseScore's anchored matching and OSMD's own
ExpressionReader.checkIfWordsNodeIsRepetitionInstruction().
Such texts are now rendered as text (e.g. UnknownExpression) again.

Also:
- accept spaces within the abbreviations, e.g. "D. S. al Fine", "D. C."
- remove an unreachable duplicate "d.c. al coda" branch

* fix(VexFlowMusicSheetCalculator): Don't overlap repetition instructions like D.S. al Coda with chord symbols (#1689)

Repetition instructions (VexFlow StaveRepetitions: Coda/Segno signs and
texts like "D.S. al Fine") were drawn at a fixed position above the
staff, without a bounding box or any skyline interaction, so they could
overlap chord symbols ("harmony texts") and each other.

Now their drawn box (replicating the positioning of the VexFlowPatch's
staverepetition.js) is checked against the skyline: if something
protrudes into the default drawing position - e.g. a chord symbol,
which is calculated before the repetition instructions - the repetition
instruction is shifted above it (setShiftY). Its space is then reserved
in the skyline, so that later placed objects and the staffline spacing
take it into account (and repetition instructions that would truly
overlap each other stack above each other).
The collision is checked with the exact estimated extents (no safety
margins), so that repetition marks with a small gap between them are
not stacked unnecessarily. For the segno sign, whose anchor is the
begin instructions width at draw time (which can still change after
this calculation), a tolerant range around that width is used.

Also, VexFlowMeasure.addWordRepetition() now returns the created
VF.Repetition and registers it in the previously unused
vfRepetitionWords list (reset with the stave in resetLayout()).

D.S. al Coda, Coda - each colliding with a chord symbol) and layout
tests for both #1688 and #1689.

fix(Slurs): Fix NaN slur curve (invalid SVG path) when a note has both a slur start and an orphan slur stop

A note carrying both a slur start and a slur stop with the same slur number
(e.g. measure 23 of the Moonlight sonata sample, a Sibelius export quirk where
the stop has no matching earlier start) let the stop close the slur just
started on that very note, creating a zero-length slur from the note to
itself. Its curve calculation then divided 0 by 0 (start-end angle, tangent
slopes) and produced NaN bezier control points, which were rendered as an
invalid SVG path, causing browser console errors:
  Error: <path> attribute d: Expected number, "... 2413.5CNaN NaN,NaN NaN,...".

Fixed on three levels:
- SlurReader: process a notations node's slur stops before its starts (a slur
  can't start and stop on the same note, so a stop always refers to an earlier
  slur), and never let a stop close a slur that started on the same note
  (ignore it like an orphan stop instead). Same guard for slide/glissando
  stops, which share the open slur dictionary.
- GraphicalSlur.calculateCurve: if start and end point (nearly) coincide, use
  a collapsed (invisible) curve instead of running the 0/0-prone calculation,
  and skip 0/0 tangent slopes against coinciding skyline points.
- VexFlowMusicSheetDrawer.drawSlur: skip slurs with non-finite bezier points
  (with a console warning) instead of emitting an invalid SVG path.

The degenerate slur was invisible before (browsers drop the invalid path), so
this only removes the errors: an image comparison over all 294 test samples
shows zero pixel changes. Adds a regression test on the Moonlight sample.

fix(Playback): Fix wrong tuplet playback duration from export errors like musx2mxl. Read tuplet note length from time-modification when <duration> is un-reduced

Some exporters (observed: musx2mxl 0.2.9) write the un-reduced type
duration for tuplet notes — a triplet eighth carries the <duration> of a
full eighth (e.g. 8 at divisions=16, where 16/3 isn't an integer) instead
of the tuplet-reduced value. InstrumentReader.getNoteDurationForTuplet()
took <duration> verbatim, so OSMD played and spaced the triplet as three
straight eighths and the measure overflowed (9/8 in a 4/4 bar). MuseScore
and other spec-conformant exporters reduce <duration>, so re-exporting the
passage "fixed" it.

Detect the un-reduced case (the written duration equals the note's dotted
type duration) and apply the time-modification ratio (normal/actual)
ourselves; otherwise keep <duration> as-is, so spec-conformant files and an
exporter's rounding are unaffected. If the heuristic ever misfired on a
correct note the ratio is ~1, making the correction a no-op. Handles
<normal-dot> too. Added getDottedNoteDurationFromTypeNode helper.

New karma tests read both encodings of the same passage identically
(triplet eighths = 1/12, following eighths = 1/8, measure sums to a full
4/4 bar). Full reader suite + all tuplet tests (nested, voice-alignment,
cross-staff, different normal-type) green.

perf(VexFlowMeasure): Scope correctNotePositions to its own measure (PR #1703). Improves performance especially for long pieces by 7% to over 40%.

correctNotePositions() runs once per graphical measure, but it iterated
Voice.VoiceEntries, which spans the entire score. Every measure therefore
re-positioned every note in the piece, making render() grow super-linearly
with score length; every pass after the first wrote the same value again.

Walk the measure's own staffEntries instead. render() gets 27-57% faster
on larger scores (24 parts x 200 measures: 11.3 s -> 5.0 s) and the SVG
output is byte-identical on 95 test scores. This also drops the
rules.GNote() lookups, since graphicalVoiceEntries already holds the
GraphicalNote objects.

The reference note now needs an explicit vfnote check: notehead() with no
argument dereferences vfnote[0], and the previous code only got away with
it because it abandoned the whole loop at the first note without one.
perf(VexFlowMeasure): scope correctNotePositions tab branch to its own measure (#1703)

perf(Glyph): Cache outline bounding boxes. Median ~20% performance gain (PR #1704)

reset() computes this.bbox with getOutlineBoundingBox(outline, scale, 0, 0),
which walks the glyph's bezier outline point by point, once per Glyph instance.
The origin is fixed at 0,0 there, so the box depends only on the outline and
the scale - and the outline array is already shared per glyph code through
cached_outline. A score with thousands of noteheads walks the same few dozen
outlines thousands of times.

Cache the four numbers on the font, next to cached_outline, and hand out a
fresh BoundingBox because callers keep a reference to it. Follows
options.cache, like loadMetrics does.

perf(Visual Regression Tests): Speed up visual regression tests to single seconds (from minutes), make cross-platform (PR #1709, #676)

Node + node-canvas reimplementation of test/Util/visual_regression.sh, which
needed bash + ImageMagick and only ran on Linux/macOS (i.e. a VM on Windows).
It produces the same visual_regression/diff/ output: results.txt, warnings.txt,

- The diff images are pixel-identical to ImageMagick's

npm scripts: test:visual, test:visual:build and test:visual:singletest now use
the .mjs by default (cross-platform). The previous bash+ImageMagick versions are

perf(NoteHead): Re-enable glyph outline caching for noteheads. Median 2% speedup (PR #1711)

NoteHead.draw passed this.id as the 6th argument of Glyph.renderGlyph,
which is its `nocache` flag. A truthy value disables the glyph outline
cache and deletes the shared cached_outline, so the outline string is
re-split on every notehead draw; and because the note-width path caches
the same glyph code with caching on, the two thrash each other every
render.

The notehead's SVG element id comes from openGroup, not from this call,
so dropping the argument leaves output byte-identical (verified: 317/317
test/data samples produce identical SVG) while removing the redundant
work. render() is ~2% faster on average, and up to ~10% on notehead-dense
scores (Telemann, Schubert, Haydn).

perf(Glyph): Memoize glyph width lookups during formatting. Median 5% speedup (PR #1712)

Flow.getGlyphProps' duration codes compute note widths as
new Glyph(code, scale).getMetrics().width, allocating a throwaway Glyph
on every call. The formatter queries these constantly: one render of
Gounod (1949 notes) constructs ~89,000 Glyphs across only 15 distinct

getMetrics().width is the cached bbox width (#1704), a pure function of
(code, point), so memoize it on the font next to cached_outline /
cached_bboxes. The nine width call sites now go through
Glyph.cachedWidth().

365 unit tests pass). render() is ~5% faster on medium/large scores, up

perf(Glyph): Cache scaled glyph outline segments for drawing. Median 2.5% speedup, 9% for largest score (PR #1713)

Glyph.renderOutline walked the glyph outline on every draw, re-coercing and
re-scaling each point (the outline is stored as a string array) and
allocating four bound context methods per call. The scaled, origin-relative
segments are constant per (outline, scale), so cache them once (keyed by the
outline array and scale) and replay them, adding the draw position per
point. This is the draw-time counterpart to #1704/#1712, which cache the
bbox and width used during formatting.

Byte-identical output: the replayed coordinates are the same floats the walk
produced, so all 317 test/data samples render identical SVG. render() is
~2.3% faster on medium/large scores, up to ~9% on glyph-dense scores
(ActorPreludeSample 9.0%, Gounod 7.3%).

perf(SkyBottomLineCalculator): Remove per-render allocations in updateLines (2-3% speedup in dense scores, PR #1714)

updateLines() runs once per staff line of every render and is the most
allocation-heavy step of the skyline calculation (the largest layout
sub-phase). Its work is pure array arithmetic, so the allocations were the
cost: push(...skyLine) per measure, a slice(...) + Math.min(...chunk) per
sub-sample chunk (tens of thousands per render), Math.max(...array) over the
whole line, and two .map() passes.

Same algorithm, no per-element allocations: concatenate by index-fill,
sub-sample each chunk with an in-place min/max scan, and remap in place.
Array.slice truncates its float bounds toward zero, which Math.trunc
reproduces, so the scanned column range - and every sub-sampled value - is
unchanged (min/max are order- and duplicate-independent).

Byte-identical SVG on all 316 renderable test/data samples (both the
geometric and raster skyline paths). updateLines itself is 6-10x faster; the
skyline-calculation phase is 11-21% faster; ~2-3% of total render on the
densest scores. Also removes the spreads that could throw RangeError on a
very wide staff line.

fix(Cursor): Fix cursor jumping backwards/off-canvas in rare cases. Skip unreliably positioned staff entries

Two kinds of staff entries carry x positions that don't reflect their
timestamp, and both used to be taken at face value when positioning the
cursor:

1. Note-less staff entries, e.g. entries only carrying a chord symbol
   (MusicXML harmony): the layout never positions them, so their
   relative x stays at the measure's left border regardless of their
   timestamp. Between a centered whole rest (timestamp at the measure
   start, drawn mid-measure) and such an entry,
   GraphicalMusicSheet.calculateXPositionFromTimestamp() interpolated
   the cursor BACKWARDS from mid-measure to the measure start
   (reproduced by the samples of issues #791, #1688, #1689).
2. Entries whose coordinates are plain garbage because their notes were
   never formatted/laid out: the tablature rests in
   test_tab_dont_switch_to_classical_from_clefinstruction.musicxml sit
   at x ~ 70000 units, which placed the stepping cursor ~700000px
   off-canvas (cursor img style e.g. "left: 716181px").

Fixes:
- New GraphicalMusicSheet.isReliableCursorXAnchor() identifies such
  entries; calculateXPositionFromTimestamp() skips them as
  interpolation anchors (via a new optional parameter on
  findClosestLeft-/RightStaffEntry() and getStaffEntry(), default off =
  unchanged behavior for other callers), and additionally clamps all
  three interpolation branches so interpolation can never go left of
  its anchor (a centered whole rest can sit right of the computed
  system border at narrow widths).
- Cursor.update() (stepping, e.g. cursor.next()) prefers reliably
  positioned entries; where every entry at the current position has
  garbage coordinates, it interpolates between the closest reliable
  neighbors via calculateXPositionFromTimestamp() instead of jumping to
  a garbage x position.

New karma tests (test/Common/OSMD/Cursor_ReliablePosition_Test.ts)
verify a monotonic timestamp->x mapping per music system on the four
chord-symbol/whole-rest samples and that stepping through the tablature
sample never leaves the page; all five fail without this fix. The new
tool test/Util/check_cursor_backwards.mjs (shared with osmd-extended,
which also uses its playback-cursor checks) scans every sample in
test/data headlessly for backwards cursor movement: the whole sample

fix(IncrementalRendering): Draw the copyright with the final batch of renderNext(), it was drawn with the first batch and left behind mid-score (SVG) or missing (Canvas) as the page grew (#1710)

An incremental render (renderNext) draws the page labels only with its first batch. The copyright
(EngravingRules.RenderCopyright, from the MusicXML <rights> element) is positioned below the last
system of the layout at that time, i.e. the not-yet-drawn system the first batch holds back, and
later batches append systems below it without moving or redrawing it. With the SVG backend the
text node ended up in the middle of the score once the page had grown (the layout model was
updated correctly, only the drawn node was stale); with the Canvas backend it was missing
altogether, because it lay beyond the canvas height at the time it was drawn and was clipped.

Now each page label is drawn with the batch that draws the system it is anchored to: the title
block (title, subtitle, composer, lyricist) with the batch drawing the first system, as before,
and the copyright only with the batch drawing the last system, the final one, once its position
is final. The copyright is marked as anchored to the page bottom by the calculator
(GraphicalLabel.AnchoredToPageBottom), so the drawer needs no knowledge of specific labels.
While the incremental render is still incomplete, no copyright is shown; it appears below the
last system with the final batch. A finished incremental render is now pixel-identical to a
normal render() (verified with the new sample: 0 differing pixels).

fix(Grace Notes): Group grace notes after their main note (Nachschlag) with the main note like grace notes before it: same staff entry and cursor step, so cursor.VoicesUnderCursor() returns them together, instead of an extra staff entry at the end of the measure (#1706)

Grace notes after the last main note of a staff in a measure - a Nachschlag, e.g.
the two small notes ending a trill, written in MusicXML as <grace/> notes after
their main note with no further note in the measure - were read into their own
SourceStaffEntry at the main note's end timestamp, i.e. at the end of the measure
(a 2/4 timestamp in a 2/4 measure): grace notes have no duration, and the reader
places every note at the current timestamp. So the cursor stopped on them in an
extra step after the main note, and cursor.VoicesUnderCursor() / NotesUnderCursor()
at the main note didn't return them (#1706) - unlike grace notes before a main
note, which are read into the main note's staff entry and cursor step.

Now they are grouped with their main note the same way: like grace notes before a
main note, each of them stays its own VoiceEntry (IsGrace; a VoiceEntry holds one
chord, so they can't become notes of the main note's VoiceEntry), but
InstrumentReader.attachGraceNotesAfterMainNote() moves them, once the measure is
read, into the SourceStaffEntry of the last main note of their voice, with its
timestamp and marked VoiceEntry.GraceAfterMainNote (which VexFlowMeasure only set
at render time before, for the grace notes left over at the end of a measure).
cursor.VoicesUnderCursor() at the main note now returns the main note's VoiceEntry
followed by the grace note VoiceEntries, NotesUnderCursor() includes the grace
notes, and the extra cursor step is gone. Grace notes followed by another main
note in the measure are not affected. The emptied staff entry and container are
dropped by the existing MusicSheetReader.checkSourceMeasureForNullEntries(). One
pass over the voice entries of the measure per staff, 1-4 µs per measure.

This also fixes the measure length: SourceMeasure.Duration is calculated from the
last staff entry's timestamp plus its note length, so the extra staff entry made
a 2/4 measure ending with 16th grace notes 9/16 long (Haydn Concertante Cello
m.90 and the octave shift sample m.3: 17/16 in 4/4), which shifted the absolute
timestamps of all following measures by a 16th.

They are still drawn as separate small notes right of the main note (own
tickables of the vexflow voice):
- VexFlowMeasure and VexFlowTabMeasure create their stand-alone notes when they
  see the flag (instead of collecting them for a GraceNoteGroup before a
  following note), skip them in the ghost rest gap filling (they take no time of
  their own) and don't attach an in-staff clef to them.
- VexFlowStaffEntry.calculateXPosition() ignores them, so they neither set the
  staff entry's x position (cursor position) nor widen its bounding box (slur
  endpoints).
- MusicSheetCalculator.createGraphicalMeasure() handles them after all other
  entries of the measure, so that accidentals, in-staff clef changes and octave
  shifts (including a stop between the grace notes, PR #1649) apply to them as
  at their drawn position, like before. The octave shift lookup per staff entry
  moved into getActiveOctaveShift() for that.
VoiceEntry.ParentSourceStaffEntry and Note.ParentStaffEntry got setters for the
move.
The only rendering difference: a measure whose first staff ends with such grace
notes no longer gets the 0.3 units of spacing that calculateMeasureXLayout()
adds per staff entry for their former extra staff entry, so it is slightly
narrower (Haydn Concertante Cello m.90 and m.196). All other samples render
identically.

fix(Iterator): Keep the enrolled timestamp consistent when moving the iterator backwards: moveToPrevious() now subtracts the measure durations it moves back over, which were only ever added, so CurrentEnrolledTimestamp no longer overstates the position after cursor.previous() and no longer grows with every cursor.update() at the end of the sheet

MusicPartManagerIterator.CurrentEnrolledTimestamp - the repetition-unrolled playback
timestamp: the durations of the measures passed so far plus the position in the
current measure - was only ever increased. recursiveMove() adds the measure's
duration when it leaves a measure forward, but recursiveMoveBack() - moveToPrevious(),
moveToPreviousVisibleVoiceEntry() and hence cursor.previous(), and the
moveToPrevious()/moveToNext() round trip cursor.update() does at the end of the sheet
to show the end of the last measure - rewound only the source position
(CurrentSourceTimestamp, the in-measure timestamp and the measure index) and never
subtracted anything. After moving back across a measure boundary the enrolled
timestamp overstated the position by the durations of the measures moved back over,
and moving forward again across the same boundary added them once more, so every
previous() + next() round trip inflated it permanently, as did every update() at the
end of the sheet (each added the last measure's duration again).
E.g. OSMD_function_Test_Repeat.musicxml (4/4, one measure = one whole note): with the
cursor at the start of measure 2 (enrolled 2, after both passes of measure 1, source
1), cursor.previous() moved to the half rest of measure 1 (source 1/2) but reported
enrolled 2 1/2 instead of 1 1/2.

Now recursiveMoveBack() subtracts what recursiveMove() added: the duration of the
measure it moves back into (the source-previous measure), and, when coming back from
the end of the sheet (recognizable by the voice entry index standing behind the last
vertical container of the last measure), the last measure's duration, which
recursiveMove() had added when it left the measure. An end reached because of
Sheet.SelectionEnd is reached at a container of a measure, without that addition, so
nothing is subtracted there.
Repetitions are still not unrolled backwards: moveToPrevious() steps to the
source-previous measure, so after moving back over a backward jump the enrolled
timestamp refers to the most recent pass of that measure - the enrolled timestamp
moves back by the same amount as the source timestamp, and which pass in the
enrolled order that is stays ambiguous. What holds now: enrolled and source
timestamps stay consistent with each other, a position reached by moving back into
the enrolled-previous measure has its correct enrolled timestamp, and moving back and
forth is neutral, both mid-sheet and at the end of the sheet.
Playback is unaffected: the PlaybackManager only moves its own iterator forward or
re-creates it.

fix(Unison): Draw the notehead of a hidden unison note (print-object="no", e.g. 8th under a half note in another voice) beside the visible head instead of leaving its beamed stem bare; center tuplet number over it (PR #1730, #1729)

MuseScore writes a unison across two voices by hiding one of the two
notes with print-object="no", so that a single notehead serves both.
Note.sharesNoteheadWithVisibleUnisonNote() recognizes that case and
keeps such a note's beam and stem, but two other sites still gated on
PrintObject alone, so the note ended up half-included in what it belongs
to.

The notehead: where Vexflow can merge the two heads into one column
(StaveNote.format -> mergeableUnison), the visible note's head stands in
for the hidden one and nothing is missing. Where it can't - a merge only
happens between heads of the same shape, so an eighth hidden under a
half note is laid out beside it - the hidden head was painted fully
transparent at a column of its own, and the beam ended on a bare stem
with nothing under it. Color it like a visible note under exactly the
condition its stem already uses, so head and stem are drawn together;
where the two heads do merge, the inked head lands on the visible one,
same glyph, same position. notehead="none" asks for no notehead at all
and stays hidden.

The tuplet: hidden or not, the note is one of the tuplet's notes. Left
out of handleTuplet(), the VF.Tuplet was built from the remaining ones
and its number centered over those - in the test sample, half a note
spacing right of the beam's center.

Debussy's Arabesque no. 1 m.3, added as a test sample, has both: a
sustained F#3 half note in voice 1 and a triplet in voice 2 whose first
eighth is the same F#3, hidden. The same encoding appears in Clair de
lune and in Liszt's Liebestraum no. 3.

Closes #1729

fix(Unison): Color the notehead drawn for a hidden unison note like the visible note whose head it shares, so it never overprints that note's color (follow-up to #1730, #1729)

Since #1730 the head of a hidden (print-object="no") beamed note that
shares a visible unison note's notehead is inked instead of transparent.
Where Vexflow merges the two heads into one column, that head lands
exactly on the visible one - after it in draw order when its voice comes
later - and took the hidden note's own color: default black. That
overprinted any color the visible note had: a red set on it by an app
highlighting the notes under the cursor, for instance (which never sees
the hidden note, cursor.NotesUnderCursor() skips invisible notes),
rendered as a black head. Verified with the Arabesque test bar with the
voice-1 note as a colored eighth (same head shape, merged column): the
hidden note's black head was drawn over the red one.

The hidden note's head now takes the color of the visible note it
shares its head with. In the merged case that makes the inked head a
no-op for any color, and where Vexflow lays the head out beside the
visible one, it's colored like the head it stands in for. For default
colors nothing changes: all samples render pixel-identical.

Note.visibleUnisonNoteSharingNotehead() returns that partner note,
sharesNoteheadWithVisibleUnisonNote() is now a shorthand for it. Test
in VexFlowMeasure_Test.ts covers the merged and the displaced case.

fix(Tempo Expressions): Render a tempo marking repeated in several parts only once instead of once per part stacked above the first system (CharlesGounod_Meditation: "Andante Simplice." 5 times), and draw rit./accel. words once instead of twice

MusicXML from part-based exporters (e.g. Finale) often repeats a tempo
marking in every part. OSMD renders all tempo expressions of a measure on
the first visible staff, so every copy was stacked above the first
system: five "Andante Simplice." in CharlesGounod_Meditation, two
"Moderato" in ActorPreludeSample. The code had an "already added?" check
for this, but its `continue` was inside the inner loop over the staff
line's expressions and never skipped anything.

calculateTempoExpressionsForMultiTempoExpression() now skips a tempo
marking when one with the same text (or, for metronome marks, the same
beat unit, bpm and dot) at the same absolute timestamp is already on the
staff line (isTempoMarkingAlreadyRendered()), before its label is
created and pushed into the skyline. The same marking at a later
position (e.g. "rit." in another measure) is unaffected.

Metronome marks were already effectively drawn once per measure, but by
accident: createMetronomeMark() used the expression's StaffNumber - the
staff within its part - as an index into the measure list, so every
part's mark landed on the first staff of the score, where the one-mark-
per-measure guard swallowed the rest, and the mark was lost when that
staff was hidden. It now draws on the first visible staff of the measure
like all other tempo markings. Each duplicate metronome entry also
registered an empty label in the skyline; without those, the first
system sits a few pixels higher in Bach_PraeludiumInCDur, the Clementi
sonatinas, ScottJoplin_The_Entertainer and the JingleBellRock sample.

Continuous tempo expressions (rit., accel., "poco meno") were pushed into
StaffLine.AbstractExpressions twice - once by the
GraphicalInstantaneousTempoExpression constructor, once explicitly - so
the drawer drew their label twice at the same spot, which made them look
bolder than other words. They are registered once now.

Dynamics are not touched: in all 311 test samples no dynamic is
duplicated within a staff or an instrument (the reader already merges a
second dynamic at the same position of a staff into one marking); the
duplicates that exist are one per instrument, which is correct in a
score.

Test: TempoExpressionDuplicates_Test.ts (Gounod: one "Andante
Simplice." on the first staff; a two-part score with the same words,
metronome mark and later "rit." in both parts: each rendered once, also
when the first part is hidden).

fix(Ties): Draw the tie of a hidden unison note at the visible note whose notehead it shares, and draw the tie of notes doubled by a hidden voice only once (follow-up to PR #1731)

PR #1731 looks a tie note up by its own GraphicalNote first, which fixes the tie of a visible note whose
notehead is shared with a hidden unison note (print-object="no") of an earlier voice. The mirrored encoding
got worse by it: when the hidden one of the two notes is the one carrying the tie, and the visible one is in
the earlier voice, the old pitch lookup happened to find the visible note and drew the tie; the own-note lookup
finds the hidden note, and handleTie() skips the tie. Which of the two notes the source hides is the engraver's
choice (with two filled heads, either gives the same picture in MuseScore), so it must not decide whether the
tie is drawn. E.g. BWV 847 m.35 with the held C2's dotted eighth hidden instead of voice 1's 16th C2: the
quarter C2 looked struck again instead of held.

- GraphicalStaffEntry.findTieGraphicalNoteFromNote(): for a hidden tie note, look up the visible note whose
  notehead it shares (Note.visibleUnisonNoteSharingNotehead()), the tie is drawn at that notehead.
- MusicSheetCalculator.handleTie(): skip a tie segment whose found notes aren't its own and are tied to each
  other themselves. That is a hidden voice doubling visible tied notes in unison (e.g. a playback-only voice):
  before PR #1731 its tie was drawn a second time at the visible notes (one tie above, one below), the PR
  stopped that, and the lookup above alone would have brought it back.

Tests (VexFlowMeasure_Test.ts): the PR's sample with the other note hidden (DOM-edited, no new file) draws all
four ties, a hidden voice doubling two tied half notes draws one tie. The PR's test uses the same helper.
All 337 visual regression samples are pixel-identical to PR #1731 (no sample has a hidden tied note).
